newsitem.title: KENYA: Central bank intervention stabilizes Kenyan unit.
newsitem.headline: Central bank intervention stabilizes Kenyan unit.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling stablized against the dollar on Wednesday after central bank intervention, commercial bank dealers said.
"There were a lot of (dollar) inflows from horticulture and foreign investors, but the central bank came in (on Tuesday afternoon) and soaked up all the excess dollars," a dealer said.
The bank posted the shilling at a mean rate of 54.87, unchanged against the dollar from Tuesday, while against the pound it was posted at a mean rate of 89.69 from 89.59.
Dealers said consistent central bank dollar demand kept the shilling at just under the 55-level as the central bank bought between 54.90 and 54.95.
"They (the central bank) have been the major buyers. Otherwise, verall demand for the dollar is low," a dealer said.
The money market was liquid with overnight rates quoted as low as 10 percent.
